I added the `bulk-refunds` flag and gated `refund()` on it. I couldn't run `refund()` itself because `structlog` isn't installed here. What I did check is that `flags.is_on("bulk-refunds")` reads the new entry and returns `False`. No existing tests reference refunds.

- **`flags.toml`**: I declared `bulk-refunds = false`. The flag has to be declared before code reads it, otherwise `is_on()` silently returns `False`.
- **`src/billing/refunds.py`**: `refund()` now checks `flags.is_on("bulk-refunds")` first. When the flag is off, it raises `RuntimeError("refunds are disabled: feature flag 'bulk-refunds' is off")`. When it's on, the original logic runs unchanged.

You didn't say what `refund()` should do when the flag is off, so I made it raise. If you'd rather it return `None` or fall back to some other behaviour, that's a small change.

With the default `false`, every `refund()` call will now raise until the flag is turned on. Check whether anything already calls it before you merge.
